summary: A single-page form shown in place of the dashboard while signed out. A script handler sends it over the application's socket; there is no POST action. With two-factor enabled the same form then asks for a token.

sources.title: Uptime Kuma 2.5.6 HiddenInput component, which renders the password input of the login component
Uptime Kuma 2.5.6 layout and router: the login component replaces every dashboard route while signed out
Uptime Kuma 1.23.16 login component, for comparison

selectors.locator: lines 19-25 use HiddenInput; source password-input lines 3-13 write the input with class form-control and bind its type, line 60 sets that type to password
selectors.note: The type starts as password and becomes text only when the user clicks the show button. Release 1.23.16 writes the input directly with type password and class form-control (source login-1x, line 13).

selectors.locator: lines 60-62; the same button submits the token

fixtures.note: The same form after the server asked for a token: the two credential fields are replaced by the token field.

staysInteractive.note: The token prompt is filled only when the user saved an authenticator secret and turned automatic 2FA on; otherwise it is typed by hand.

schemaGaps: The path gate names paths at the host root, and the format has no installation-relative gate. An installation under a sub-path is not covered. Nothing is filled there.
notes: In 2.5.6 the id floatingPassword is given to the HiddenInput component and not written on its input, so no selector relies on it. The container, form, username id, a password-type input with class form-control, the otp id and the submit button are also in the login component of 1.18.5, 1.21.3, 1.23.16 and 2.0.0 (read at those tags on 2026-10-12); older releases were not read. The setup page at /setup reuses the two ids and is outside the path gate. An instance with authentication disabled shows no form.
